## Aim 

The aim of the Overrepresentation Analysis (ORA) is to determine whether specific functional gene sets are statistically overrepresented among genes identified as significant by the differential gene expression analysis, compared with the background set of genes eligible for selection.

1\) Loading the Libraries

```{r}
# Loading Libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(msigdbr)
library(fgsea)

# Setting the significance threshold at 5% FDR
alpha <- 0.05
```

## **\## GSE67333**

1\) Loading DESeq2 Results – GSE67333 dataset

```{r}
# Defining the path to the complete DESeq2 results for GSE67333
file_67333 <- "results/DESeq2GSE67333/DESeq2_all_genes.csv"

# Checking that the DESeq2 result file exists in the specified path
file.exists(file_67333)

# Loading the complete DESeq2 results into R
res_67333 <- read.csv(file_67333)

# Checking the dimensions of the DESeq2 result table
dim(res_67333)

# Checking the available columns in the DESeq2 result table
colnames(res_67333)

# Inspecting the first rows of the DESeq2 result table
head(res_67333)
```

2\) Inspecting the gene IDs

```{r}
# Inspecting the first gene IDs in the DESeq2 results
head(res_67333$gene_id)
# The DESeq2 gene identifiers were inspected and were already formatted as Ensembl gene IDs without version suffixes. Therefore, no additional gene ID cleaning was required.
```

3\) Preparing Gene Ontology Gene Sets

```{r}
# Retrieving Biological Process gene sets from MSigDB
BP_df <- msigdbr(
  species = "Homo sapiens",
  category = "C5",
  subcategory = "BP"
)

# Converting Biological Process gene sets into the named list required by fora()
BP_list <- split(
  x = BP_df$ensembl_gene,
  f = BP_df$gs_name
)

# Retrieving Molecular Function gene sets from MSigDB
MF_df <- msigdbr(
  species = "Homo sapiens",
  category = "C5",
  subcategory = "MF"
)

# Converting Molecular Function gene sets into the named list required by fora()
MF_list <- split(
  x = MF_df$ensembl_gene,
  f = MF_df$gs_name
)

# Retrieving Cellular Component gene sets from MSigDB
CC_df <- msigdbr(
  species = "Homo sapiens",
  category = "C5",
  subcategory = "CC"
)

# Converting Cellular Component gene sets into the named list required by fora()
CC_list <- split(
  x = CC_df$ensembl_gene,
  f = CC_df$gs_name
)
```

```{r}
# Inspecting the Biological Process gene-set table
head(BP_df)

# Checking the structure of the Biological Process gene-set list
str(BP_list, max.level = 1)

# Checking how many Biological Process gene sets were retrieved
length(BP_list)

# Inspecting the first Biological Process gene set
head(BP_list, 1)

```

4\) Defining Background and Target

```{r}
# Keeping genes with an available adjusted p-value
tested_67333 <- res_67333 |>
  filter(!is.na(padj))

# Defining the ORA background as all genes eligible for selection
background_67333 <- unique(tested_67333$gene_id)

# Defining the ORA target as genes significant at FDR < 0.05
target_67333 <- unique(
  tested_67333$gene_id[
    tested_67333$padj < alpha
  ]
)

# Checking the number of genes in the background
length(background_67333)

# Checking the number of significant genes in the target
length(target_67333)
```

5\) Running Overrepresentation Analysis

##The ORA background was defined as the genes with an available DESeq2 adjusted p-value, representing the genes eligible for selection. Genes with an adjusted p-value below 0.05 were defined as the target gene set.

```{r}
# Running ORA for Biological Process gene sets
ora_BP_67333 <- fora(
  BP_list,
  target_67333,
  background_67333
)

# Running ORA for Molecular Function gene sets
ora_MF_67333 <- fora(
  MF_list,
  target_67333,
  background_67333
)

# Running ORA for Cellular Component gene sets
ora_CC_67333 <- fora(
  CC_list,
  target_67333,
  background_67333
)
```

```{r}
# Inspecting the ORA result columns
colnames(ora_BP_67333)

# Inspecting the first Biological Process ORA results
head(ora_BP_67333)
```

6\) Calculating Relative Enrichment

\## Relative enrichment was calculated for each GO term to quantify how strongly significant genes were overrepresented relative to the background gene set.

```{r}
# Creating a function to calculate the relative enrichment of each GO term
compute_enrichment <- function(ora, n_genes, n_universe) {
  
  # Calculating the relative risk for each GO term
  ora$relative_risk <-
    (ora$overlap / ora$size) /
    (n_genes / n_universe)
  
  # Returning the ORA results with the new relative_risk column
  return(ora)
}

# Calculating relative enrichment for Biological Process results
ora_BP_67333 <- compute_enrichment(
  ora_BP_67333,
  length(target_67333),
  length(background_67333)
)

# Calculating relative enrichment for Molecular Function results
ora_MF_67333 <- compute_enrichment(
  ora_MF_67333,
  length(target_67333),
  length(background_67333)
)

# Calculating relative enrichment for Cellular Component results
ora_CC_67333 <- compute_enrichment(
  ora_CC_67333,
  length(target_67333),
  length(background_67333)
)

# Inspecting the Biological Process results
head(ora_BP_67333)
```

7\) Significantly Enriched GO Terms

```         
```

```{r}
# Selecting significant Biological Process GO terms
sig_BP_67333 <- ora_BP_67333 |>
  filter(padj < alpha) |>
  arrange(padj, pval)

# Selecting significant Molecular Function GO terms
sig_MF_67333 <- ora_MF_67333 |>
  filter(padj < alpha) |>
  arrange(padj, pval)

# Selecting significant Cellular Component GO terms
sig_CC_67333 <- ora_CC_67333 |>
  filter(padj < alpha) |>
  arrange(padj, pval)

# Selecting the top 10 significant Biological Process GO terms
top10_BP_67333 <- head(sig_BP_67333, 10)

# Selecting the top 10 significant Molecular Function GO terms
top10_MF_67333 <- head(sig_MF_67333, 10)

# Selecting the top 10 significant Cellular Component GO terms
top10_CC_67333 <- head(sig_CC_67333, 10)

# Displaying the top 10 results
top10_BP_67333
top10_MF_67333
top10_CC_67333
```

```{r}
# Cheking how many significant terms there are in total
nrow(sig_BP_67333)
nrow(sig_MF_67333)
nrow(sig_CC_67333)
```

```{r}
# Displaying the significant Molecular Function GO term
sig_MF_67333

# Displaying all significant Cellular Component GO terms
sig_CC_67333
```

\
8) Results

-   No **Biological Process** GO terms reached significance at FDR \< 0.05

-   The only significantly enriched **Molecular Function** term was oxidoreduction-driven active transmembrane transporter activity (adjusted p-value = 0.030). Four of the significant differentially expressed genes were associated with this term, which showed approximately 26-fold enrichment relative to the background. This indicates that genes involved in this pathway are overrepresented among the differentially expressed genes in the GSE67333 Alzheimer’s disease dataset.

-   11 **Cellular Component** GO terms were significantly enriched in GSE67333. The enriched terms formed two main patterns. Several terms were associated with membrane and transporter protein complexes, indicating an overrepresentation of differentially expressed genes in membrane-associated cellular structures. A more specific group of terms was related to mitochondrial respiratory machinery, including the respirasome, oxidoreductase complexes, inner mitochondrial membrane protein complexes and respiratory chain complex III. An additional significant term involved the MHC class II protein complex.

8\) Results - Biological Interpretation

-   Three **Molecular Function** GO terms were significantly enriched in GSE173955. The strongest enrichment was observed for T-cell receptor binding, with four overlapping genes and approximately 101-fold enrichment relative to the background. More broadly, signaling receptor binding and protein-containing complex binding were also significantly enriched, suggesting that receptor-associated and protein-binding molecular functions are overrepresented among the differentially expressed genes.

-   **Biological Process** enrichment showed a strong immune related pattern. The top enriched terms were associated with T-cell activation and proliferation, lymphocyte activation, and leukocyte cell-cell adhesion. Overall, the results indicate that genes involved in T-cell and lymphocyte-related immune processes are strongly overrepresented among the differentially expressed genes in GSE173955.

-   **Cellular Component** enrichment showed significant overrepresentation of membrane associated and immune related structures. Several enriched terms were related to the MHC protein complex, immunological synapse, and plasma membrane protein complexes. Additional enriched terms involved ER-to-Golgi transport and vesicle-associated membrane structures.

**Α small overview of Ora results in both datasets**

**ORA of the DESeq2 results from GSE67333** identified enrichment mainly at the Molecular Function and Cellular Component levels. The enriched terms were associated with membrane and transporter protein complexes, as well as mitochondrial respiratory structures, and inner mitochondrial membrane protein complexes. An additional enriched Cellular Component term involved the MHC class II protein complex. No significant Biological Process terms were identified. Overall, the results suggest that the differential expression signal in GSE67333 is particularly associated with membrane-related and mitochondrial respiratory cellular components.

**ORA of the age- and sex-adjusted DESeq2** results revealed a strong immune-related enrichment pattern in **GSE173955.** Biological Process terms were mainly associated with T-cell and lymphocyte activation and proliferation, while Molecular Function enrichment highlighted T-cell receptor and signaling receptor binding. Cellular Component terms included the MHC protein complex, immunological synapse, and other membrane-associated structures. Together, these results suggest that immune-related, particularly T-cell-associated, functions are strongly overrepresented among the differentially expressed genes in this dataset.

The two datasets did not show exactly the same enriched GO terms, but both showed signals related to immune functions and membrane-associated processes. This may mean that these changes are more consistently linked to Alzheimer’s disease across the two datasets.
